definition: Reactive coping is a coping style, contrasted with proactive coping, that describes a characteristic way an individual responds to stress. In this source, it is linked to different patterns of immune activity than a proactive coping style.

reasons: The packet shows a coping-style comparison in pigs, but it does not define reactive coping as a general characteristic way an individual responds to stress.
The statement that reactive coping is 'contrasted with proactive coping' is only partly supported by the study’s comparison of coping styles; it is not presented as a dictionary definition.
The claim that reactive coping is 'linked to different patterns of immune activity' is supported only for this pig study and should not be generalized as a broader definitional feature.

The packet mentions “coping style” with categories described as “proactive” and “reactive,” but it does not define what “reactive coping” specifically means as a coping style (e.g., the behavioral/psychological characteristics of reactive coping).

The packet supports that coping style is linked to differences in immune measures (e.g., alternative complement activity and KLH antibody titers), but the definition’s claim that reactive coping is “contrasted with proactive coping” as a general coping style concept is only partially supported without an explicit definition of “reactive coping.”

The definition asserts a broad “characteristic way an individual responds to stress,” yet the packet only reports associations between coping style and immune status in pigs rather than describing the stress-response pattern that characterizes reactive coping.
